title: Stove — Database Health
description: Application and database health, HTTP latency, process resources, pending ingestion, streams, workers, database growth and contention for stove-server.

options.content: **Choose your Prometheus data source, job, and server instance above.** The **App** section shows HTTP traffic, process resources, pending ingestion, streams, worker health, and retention. Process resource panels require Linux. Expand **SQLite** or **PostgreSQL** for database health, growth, performance, and diagnostics; each section filters its own backend. Database sizes are shown per instance; PostgreSQL replicas can report the same database, so do not add their sizes together. Check collector freshness before interpreting diagnostics. Unsupported or unavailable metrics show **No data**. Quiet ingestion is normal. Growth is a trend, not a capacity guarantee; retention can free reusable pages without shrinking files.

panels.title: HTTP requests / second
panels.description: Responses by route and status. Metrics scrapes are excluded; unmatched paths share one label.

panels.title: HTTP latency p95 / p99
panels.description: Time until response headers, including request-body extraction. SSE body lifetime is measured separately by active streams.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, instance, stove_instance, route, method) (rate(stove_app_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, instance, stove_instance, route, method) (rate(stove_app_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: HTTP errors and cancellations / second
panels.description: HTTP 4xx, 5xx and handlers cancelled before response headers, grouped by route and status. Malformed protobuf bodies appear as 4xx.

panels.title: HTTP requests in flight
panels.description: Handlers awaiting response headers, excluding scrapes. Persistent SSE streams appear in Active streams.

panels.title: Process CPU usage
panels.description: Linux Prometheus process collector. CPU seconds/second equals utilized CPU cores; 1.0 means one core. Container CPU limits require infrastructure metrics.

panels.title: Process resident memory
panels.description: Linux process resident memory. Compare with pod/container limits in infrastructure monitoring.

panels.title: Ingestion in flight
panels.description: Unfinished decoded event attempts, including preparation and database waits. Stove commits inline with no separate ingestion queue; producer and network buffers are not measured.

panels.title: Oldest pending ingestion event
panels.description: Age of the oldest unfinished ingestion attempt. Rising age with DB acquisition latency reveals a blocked write; zero means idle.

panels.title: Ingestion processing latency p95 / p99
panels.description: Event preparation through commit for HTTP and gRPC, including validation and database waits.

panels.title: Ingestion outcomes / second
panels.description: Accepted, duplicate, and failed decoded-event attempts. Malformed HTTP protobuf bodies are counted as HTTP 4xx before ingestion.

panels.title: Active streams
panels.description: Live SSE response bodies and gRPC ingestion streams. These are application streams, not underlying TCP connections.

panels.title: Stream failures and lag / second
panels.description: SSE cursor/replay failures and gRPC receive errors. Lag counts missed broadcast events that trigger durable replay, not necessarily lost events.

panels.title: Background worker failures / second
panels.description: Failed collector attempts, relay polls, or notification connections, including panics/cancellation. PostgreSQL listener failures fall back to polling.

panels.title: Background worker freshness
panels.description: Time since successful work or listener heartbeat. Zero timestamps mean the worker has never succeeded. The startup-only cursor task is excluded. Normal collector interval is 30 seconds.

panels.title: Runtime scheduling delay p95 / p99
panels.description: Delay of a one-second Tokio heartbeat. High delay indicates runtime scheduling pressure. Pair with heartbeat freshness to detect stalls with no new observations.

panels.title: Runs deleted in selected range
panels.description: Committed automatic retention and explicit purges. Clear-all and arbitrary explorer SQL are excluded.

panels.title: Retention latency p95
panels.description: Combined automatic retention work per enclosing transaction.

panels.title: Time since last successful retention
panels.description: Absent before first success. A long gap can be normal if no eligible activity triggers retention.

panels.title: Database access by role
panels.description: A read through each connection role. Check probe age below; this does not perform a synthetic write.

panels.title: Diagnostics collection
panels.description: Whether the latest diagnostic attempt succeeded. Check freshness below to detect stalled workers.

panels.title: Current database size
panels.description: PostgreSQL database-wide size including indexes; replicas can report the same database. Cached diagnostics may be stale.

panels.title: Database growth rate
panels.description: Linear size trend over the selected growth window. Positive means allocated size is growing; reusable pages and retention must also be considered.

panels.title: Blocked sessions
panels.description: Database-wide sessions waiting on a lock; needs pg_read_all_stats or equivalent.

panels.title: Oldest transaction
panels.description: Database-wide oldest transaction, excluding the collector. Needs visibility into session statistics.

panels.title: Deadlocks / second
panels.description: Database-wide PostgreSQL counter, which may reset independently of Stove. Do not sum across Stove replicas.

panels.title: Estimated dead tuples
panels.description: Estimated dead tuples across tables in the current schema.

panels.title: Time since most recent autovacuum
panels.description: Most recent autovacuum among current-schema tables. Does not show whether every table was vacuumed; absent before any recorded autovacuum.

panels.title: Session diagnostics visibility
panels.description: UP means the collector can inspect session statistics. DOWN means unavailable, often because pg_read_all_stats has not been granted.

panels.title: Operation latency p95
panels.description: Includes connection and instrumented advisory-lock acquisition waits.

panels.title: Execution latency p95
panels.description: Subtracts instrumented acquisition waits. Includes SQL execution, other database lock waits, and commit.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, instance, role, operation) (rate(stove_db_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",backend="postgresql",kind="wait"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Operation failure ratio
panels.description: No value when there are no operations. Explorer SQL errors also count as operation failures.

targets.expr: sum by (instance, role) (rate(stove_db_errors_total{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",backend="postgresql",kind="operation"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (instance, role) (rate(stove_db_duration_seconds_count{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",backend="postgresql",kind="operation"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Timeouts / second
panels.description: Uses operation-level failures to avoid double-counting waits and execution measurements.

panels.title: Connection occupancy
panels.description: Application PostgreSQL pool capacity by role.

panels.title: Waiting acquisitions
panels.description: Live count of waiting connection/mutex/advisory-lock acquisitions.

panels.title: Collector sample age
panels.description: Capacity samples every 10 seconds; diagnostics every 30 seconds. Ages over 45 and 90 seconds respectively indicate stale collection.

panels.title: Availability probe age
panels.description: Probes run every 30 seconds; age over 90 seconds indicates stale results.

panels.title: Database access by role
panels.description: A read through each connection role. Check probe age below; this does not perform a synthetic write.

panels.title: Diagnostics collection
panels.description: Whether the latest diagnostic attempt succeeded. Check freshness below to detect stalled workers.

panels.title: Current database size
panels.description: SQLite database pages excluding WAL. Cached diagnostics may be stale.

panels.title: Database growth rate
panels.description: Linear size trend over the selected growth window. Positive means allocated size is growing; reusable pages and retention must also be considered.

panels.title: SQLite filesystem available
panels.description: Space available to Stove on the database filesystem. PostgreSQL capacity requires host/cloud metrics.

panels.title: SQLite WAL size
panels.description: WAL files can remain large after checkpointing because SQLite reuses them.

panels.title: SQLite estimated days until disk full
panels.description: Available space divided by its decline over the growth window. Includes all users of this filesystem, not just Stove. No data when space is flat/increasing or diagnostics are unavailable/stale. Extrapolation only; use host/cloud monitoring for PostgreSQL.

panels.title: Reusable database pages
panels.description: Space reusable within the database file; deletion does not necessarily shrink the file.

panels.title: WAL frames awaiting checkpoint
panels.description: Current WAL frames minus checkpointed frames. These counts can reset when WAL is recycled. The NOOP probe does not checkpoint pages.

panels.title: Checkpoint counter probe
panels.description: Availability of SQLite WAL checkpoint statistics. Does not trigger checkpointing.

panels.title: Operation latency p95
panels.description: Includes connection and instrumented advisory-lock acquisition waits.

panels.title: Execution latency p95
panels.description: Subtracts instrumented acquisition waits. Includes SQL execution, other database lock waits, and commit.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, instance, role, operation) (rate(stove_db_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",backend="sqlite",kind="wait"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Operation failure ratio
panels.description: No value when there are no operations. Explorer SQL errors also count as operation failures.

targets.expr: sum by (instance, role) (rate(stove_db_errors_total{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",backend="sqlite",kind="operation"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (instance, role) (rate(stove_db_duration_seconds_count{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",backend="sqlite",kind="operation"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Timeouts and SQLite busy errors / second
panels.description: Uses operation-level failures to avoid double-counting waits and execution measurements.

panels.title: Connection occupancy
panels.description: One mutex-protected SQLite connection per role.

panels.title: Waiting acquisitions
panels.description: Live count of waiting connection/mutex/advisory-lock acquisitions.

panels.title: Collector sample age
panels.description: Capacity samples every 10 seconds; diagnostics every 30 seconds. Ages over 45 and 90 seconds respectively indicate stale collection.

panels.title: Availability probe age
panels.description: Probes run every 30 seconds; age over 90 seconds indicates stale results.
